evidence.text:
Reasonfor referral: Evaluation of exertional breathlessness that has gradually increased
over the past three months.

Findings: Sinus bradycardia at 52 bpm. Normal axis. PR interval 190 ms, QRS 97 ms, QTc 445
ms.
Impression: Sinus bradycardia, otherwise normal tracing.
TTE: LVEF 45%, mildly reduced LV fxn, no sig valve dz.

LIPID PANEEL
Total Cholesterol: 230 mg/dL (H)
LDL Cholesterol: 152 mg/dL (H)
HDL Cholesterol: 53 mg/dL
Triglycerides: 129 mg/dL

BASIC METABOLIC PANEL
Sodium: 136 mmol/L
Potassium: 4.9 mmol/L
Chloride: 98 mmol/L
CO2: 21 mmol/L
BUN: 20 mg/dL
Creatinine: 0.7 mg/dL
Glucose: 161 mg/dL (H)
Calcium: 9.1 mg/dL

Lisinopril 10 mg by mouth once daily
Metformin 500 mg by mouth twice daily
Levothyroxine 75 mcg by mouth once daily

EXAM:
General: comfortable at rest.
Neck: supple, no jugular venous distension.
Cardiac exam: regular rate and rhythm, normal S1 and S2, soft systolic murmur at the
sternal border, no gallop.
Lungs: clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Extremities: no peripheral edema.

General: comfortable at rest.
Neck: no jugular venous distension.
Cardiac exam: regular rate and rhythm, normal S1 and S2, no murmurs, rubs, or gallops.
Lungs:clear bilaterally.
Extremities: 1+ pitting edema of both ankles.
